exact_statement: For a-bit addressing A_a, a>=1, padded to N>=a+2^a, the fixed binary selector/data/padding hierarchy all-subset prefix code has Gamma_T(A_a)=3+2a+2R(a)+2*1{N>a+2^a}, where R(1)=0 and R(k)=1-2^{-k}+R(floor(k/2))+R(ceil(k/2)), and Gamma_T(A_a)<=8I(A_a)-5. Every Boolean truth-table edit f of density rho obeys H(f)<=Gamma_T(f)<=16I(f)-10+48N*rho-8rho. Thus N*rho<=1/8 gives <=16I(f), and every one-point edit gives <=25I(f), with <=16I(f) for N>=6. For any Boolean g on a split cube Z union Y with r=|Z|>=1 and |Y|>=1, join fixed binary singleton-leaf trees on Z,Y, put W_Z,W_Y for their internal-mask costs, and flip g on z=z*. Writing rho=2^{-r}, h=g(z*,.), m_h=Eh and U_Z=sum_v 2(1-2^{-|C_v|}), the exact difference-spectrum cost is E_delta=4rho[1+2(1-rho*m_h^2)+U_Z+E_{S_h}W_Y]. Partial restriction Parseval gives rho*E_{S_h}W_Y<=E_{S_g}W_Y, hence E_delta<=4E_{S_g}W_Y+4rho(2r+1) and Gamma_T(f)<=2Gamma_T(g)+8E_{S_g}W_Y+8rho(2r+1). Free-coordinate influences are unchanged, and I_Z(f)+I_Z(g)>=2r*rho.
hypotheses: Actual Boolean signs on the uniform finite cube; entropy and code lengths in bits.
I is total physical pivotal influence, equal to sum_S |S| fhat(S)^2.
Trees and child coordinate order are fixed before the Fourier subset is sampled.
L_T(S)=1+sum internal b_v*1{S meets C_v}; all masks and the root/empty bit are retained.
Addressing family has distinct physical data coordinates, a>=1; arbitrary edits flip inherited values.
Subcube energy identities require the tree root to separate nonempty Z,Y; h is retained without a universal core-cost assumption.
No universal FEI or Gamma<=C I conclusion is asserted for arbitrary subcube edits.
